Note that you can use LEgacy's power to buff himself and then hit something if you have the Legacy Ring out - this lets you use two powers. So use the first as Galvanise, and the second as Motivational Charge if you've got it out...I don't think he has any other powers which involve hitting someone else. Also, someone like the Argent Adept can use his powers to let other heroes use their own powers/play cards/draw cards.

I did have a thought the other day, when playing as the Adept in a team with Legacy. You can only use a power once per turn, right? But if it's another hero's turn, you can use that same power again if they have the ability to let you. For example, Ra uses Blazing Tornado to nuke something, then the Adept takes his turn and lets Ra use Blazing Tornado again because it's not Ra's turn any more, but the Adept's. So can you get Legacy to play Galvanise again and get an extra bonus to damage? I'm guessing this will be a "no" because the new Galvanise just overrides the old one. But still, it'd be cool (if tremendously overpowered) were things otherwise :D.

Pretty much, you want Argent Adept to go after everyone but Bunker,Omni-tronks, and maybe Unity.

 

People like Legacy, Scholar, Mister Fixer, and Haka benefit from cards that go away at the start of their turns, so having AA go first denies you the opportunity to play them after your turn. On the other hand, Fanatic, Omni-tronks, Bunker, and (kind of) Unity benefit from cards that ACTIVATE at the start of their turns (components, zealous offense, gatling gun, supply crate) so playing them before their turn but after the villain turn is nice.

posts.name: Cosmonaut Zero
posts.cooked:
You played it right. The time when that doesn't work is when the Environment or Villain plays a card that prevents you from dealing damage. If Legacy is last and uses Galvanize and the environment flips a card that says "Heroes cannot use powers," then you kinda just wasted that Galvanize. The buff is still in effect, but you're not in a position to utilize it.

For this reason, I find that heroes that boost other heroes like to go first. That way you have the most information about the effects of your boost before you activate it and there's no craziness that can interfere with it this round. Also if you have draws it's nice to have the cards in hand to use this round instead of having to wait through an extra villain phase. I also find that heroes who debuff the villain like to go last becuase there's less computation and coordination involved in seeing what effect your actions will have.

Usually I'll be first or last so that I can manage the villain and environment turns in a row with mine. I generally play fairly efficiently and have the most experience with the game amongst my friends so the duty typically falls to me. This also means that we don't really try that hard to put all the heroes in their optimal spots because I like playing Ra as much as the next guy. I mean, if we were playing on advanced with a bunch of experienced players and Legacy really wants to get the damage boost out so that we can wipe the villain's setup minions on turn 1 instead of turn 2 then it absolutely does make a difference. But I often play with some inexperienced players and we rarely care to be that hardcore about it. Minmaxing can be fun from time to time, it just doesn't happen to be how I usually interact with SotM.

posts.name: Cosmonaut Zero
posts.cooked:
Oh the villains are most definitely meant to represent a range of difficulties. It seems that they fold in some consideration of complexity, but difficulty is a major factor.

If you're finding the game easy try skipping straight to one of the harder villains and see what happens. I actually like to introduce the game to new players by playing once against Blade, Ambuscade or Omnitron depending on what they're interested in, and then for the next game toss them at somebody really brutal like The Organization, The Martiarch or Advanced Ennead. The idea is to set us up for a loss or narrow victory. Whether we win or lose that second game, for my friends at least it tends to energize them about the game rather than demoralize them, especially if we just came off a really easy win.

If you only have the base set, maybe try Dawn? I find her more fun than Voss, personally. The times I've lost against Voss have usually been when he pulled every minion in his deck with Forced Deployment and we just couldn't burn through them in time. Which can feel kinda cheap and I probably wouldn't want that to happen in somebody's second game. When I've lost against Dawn, it's generally been a feeling of getting slowly overwhelmed by her Citizens, which actually feels really cool and fair and winnable. She's easily my favorite villain in the base set because her mechanics are really varied but still thematic, and tactical play pays off big.

posts.cooked:
The thing with Devastating Aurora is that because it nukes all your stuff, you're basically back to square one with regards to your set-up. Not so bad with someone like Tachyon, who has a grand total of one piece of equipment and three Ongoings, but someone like the Adept or Ab'Zero is bascially buggered when this occurs. Meanwhile Dawn's still got citizens in play/coming out/being rezzed and unless you have some good one-shots (or copies of stuff you just lost) in-hand you're gonna take a while before you can do anything. Having the combo of Citizen Sweat and Citizen Tears in play really is nasty as well, since one forces everyone to discard a card (two if they're both in play) and the other forces hero Ongoing destruction (one Ongoing or all of a hero's Ongoings, depending on whether both these guys are in play). If Citizen Blood comes out, that completes the trio and while Blood on his own deals damage, he adds a damage component to the other who, who I think boost his damage themselves.

Really, to best kick Dawn's arse, some form of Ongoing destruction is essential (so that citizens can actually stay dead and you don't end up with two "Return with the Dawn" cards bringing them back every turn…trust me, that's bloody annoying), as is some kind of deck control so you can find the really horrible cards (Devastating Aurora, for example) and put them to the bottom of the deck or whatever. So someone like the Wraith, Nightmist, or the Visionary would be a good start to have in your team. If you can keep up the damage (killing Citizens ASAP), take out Ongoings quickly, and prevent any Auroras from coming out, you shouldn't have too much trouble. Unless you kill five or more citizens which will cause Dawn to flip and be invincible until a certain number (think it's H-2 or something) of citizens are in play. At least she only flips once per game.

Also, Citizen Anvil is Christopher ;).

With all that said about Dawn, I fervently agree that the Matriarch is a total…well, if I said the word I'd probably get banned forever and ever but you get the idea ;).
